conviction_note: The freshest hard data I could find that is not in wire copy is a gap in C3.ai's own-name federal contract obligations for all of August 2026 (-2.5), partly offset by a company-ATS record showing a defense/intelligence rebuild being genuinely staffed (+1.5) and dragged by an uncovered board-departure cluster disclosed six days ago (-1.0); I hold the net small because the negative direction agrees with the +19 vol-point skew and with six of eight prior prints, so most of it is already paid for, and because the June guidance reset to $50-54M from $70.3M a year ago leaves a floored bar with 32% of float short.

findings.finding: FPDS-NG shows ZERO federal contract actions under 'C3.AI, INC.' signed between 2026-08-01 and 2026-09-02, against 3 actions in Aug 2025 (~$4.38M: $150.5k MDA 8/8, $0 USAF 8/18, $4.231M Army 8/27) and 3 in Aug 2024 - a break in the pattern in the month agencies obligate ahead of the 30 Sept federal year end, and the reported quarter itself contained only three actions, one of which was a 2026-07-03 DOE modification captioned 'DEOBLIGATE FUNDING AND DESCOPE REMAINING WORK' (-$625,000).
findings.source_date: 2026-09-02 (live query; comparison windows retrieved from the same feed at https://www.fpds.gov/ezsearch/FEEDS/ATOM?FEEDNAME=PUBLIC&templateName=1.5.3&q=VENDOR_FULL_NAME%3A%22C3.AI%2C+INC.%22+SIGNED_DATE%3A%5B2025%2F08%2F01%2C2025%2F09%2F30%5D&sortBy=SIGNED_DATE&desc=Y)
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates FPDS by C3.ai fiscal quarter, and the sell-side federal datapoint in circulation is management's own '+85-89% federal bookings YoY' from prior calls, which is a backward-looking bookings figure the company chooses to disclose. If the market had read the raw obligation record it would not be treating federal as the unambiguous bright spot into a guidance print: the coverage would carry a quarterly obligation series, and the Q2 FY27 guide would have a visibly wider published range. Guidance for the federal-year-end quarter is set tonight, and this is the only pre-release read on it. Caveat I will not hide: FPDS reporting lags for DoD Other Transaction Agreements, and C3 explicitly routes Intelligence Community sales through the AWS Marketplace, which never appears in FPDS under its own vendor name - both would produce a false zero, which is why the band runs to +1.
findings.independence: Same direction from a different source: across the whole reported quarter (2026-05-01 to 2026-07-31) C3 issued exactly one customer announcement, the 2026-06-04 Shell expansion, and no new customer name in the four months since - https://www.stocktitan.net/news/AI/ . That is a separate document from FPDS, but it is thematically the same claim (thin deal flow), so treat the pair as one source cluster rather than two independent negatives.

findings.finding: C3's own Greenhouse ATS lists 67 open roles of which 11 are federal/defense-titled or Tysons, Virginia-based, including a newly created 'Senior Director, Product Management - C3 AI Defense and Intelligence', a 'Senior Director, Strategic Solutions - Intelligence Community', 'Senior Director, Strategic Solutions, Navy and Maritime Industrial Base', a dedicated 'Senior/Lead Site Reliability Engineer - Federal', and - the concrete tell - a second 'Executive Assistant to the CEO' posting based in Tysons, Virginia; 5 of the 9 quota-facing 'Strategic Solutions' openings are defense or intelligence specific, and 13 postings are Palantir-style 'Forward Deployed Engineer'/'Director, Forward Deployed Engineering' roles across New York, Chicago, Atlanta, Houston, London, Redwood City and Tysons.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the company's applicant-tracking API, not a press release; it is the difference between a strategy being narrated and a strategy being funded with headcount, and no analyst preview counts C3's requisitions by title. If it were priced, the coverage into this print would frame AI as a defense-AI repositioning story with a Palantir-style forward-deployed delivery model and a DC-based CEO office, and the stock would not be sitting 46% below its 52-week high on a 180 IV with puts bid 19 points over calls - a defense/intelligence re-rating narrative is the one thing that changes this multiple, and the market is not paying for the option that Siebel frames tonight's call around it.
findings.independence: Points the same way from a different source: the two largest 2026 obligations in the FPDS record are DoD - $14,125,000 from the Missile Defense Agency on 2026-05-05 and a $15,466,382 Production Other Transaction Agreement order on 2026-04-30 - while the only shrinking relationship is DOE (https://www.fpds.gov/ezsearch/FEEDS/ATOM?FEEDNAME=PUBLIC&templateName=1.5.3&q=VENDOR_FULL_NAME%3A%22C3.AI%2C+INC.%22+SIGNED_DATE%3A%5B2026%2F02%2F01%2C2026%2F04%2F30%5D&sortBy=SIGNED_DATE&desc=Y). Note honestly that this shares the FPDS cluster with finding 1 and cuts against it: capacity and intent are being built for defense while the August obligation record is empty. Both readings can be true on different horizons, and I have sized them to partly offset rather than stacking them.

findings.finding: The DEF 14A filed 2026-08-28 discloses that Condoleezza Rice, a director since 2009 and the company's most prominent Washington name, is not standing for re-election, and that Jim Hagemann Snabe is on a leave of absence from the board and also not standing - eleven weeks after C3 issued a press release celebrating Snabe's appointment as European Commission Special Envoy for Industrial AI - while the replacement director appointed 2026-08-25 with a $900,000 option grant, John C. Dwyer, is a high-stakes litigation partner at Cooley from 1998 to 2023 and a former Acting Associate Attorney General, seated alongside a brand-new General Counsel granted 826,901 RSUs effective 2026-07-30.
findings.why_not_priced: Searches for Rice's departure return no news coverage at all - only stale profile pages still listing her as a director - which is the observable test: if this were priced there would be a wire story and the IR board page would have been updated. It matters more than routine board churn because it lands in the same week as the print and in the same direction as finding 2's subject: the company is re-centring on defense and intelligence while shedding both of the directors who carried its government standing, and the seat is being backfilled with litigation and DOJ expertise rather than defense or commercial expertise, which together with a fresh GC on an unusually large inducement grant is a legal-posture build, not a growth build. Small size because board slates almost never move a print by themselves.
findings.independence: Partly independent: the Dwyer appointment and his grant come from a separate 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001577526/000157752626000103/ai-20260825.htm (2026-08-27), and the GC inducement grant from https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260804361676/en/C3-AI-Announces-New-Employee-Inducement-Grant (2026-08-04). Dwyer appears in both the 8-K and the proxy, so those two overlap; the inducement-grant release does not.

Insider transactions - Siebel's August sales (139,500 shares at $9.61 on 08-03; 453,314 at $10.51 on 08-11) are all under a Rule 10b5-1 plan dated 2024-09-20, so they carry no information about this print
The securities class action dismissed in its entirety on 2026-07-14 (8-K item 8.01) - real but disclosed seven weeks ago and therefore priced

FY2027 executive incentive targets in the proxy - the CD&A section did not yield any numeric revenue, bookings or ARR target, and the share count requested in the 2020 Equity Incentive Plan amendment sits in an appendix I could not extract
Wayback Machine history for the Greenhouse board, to date the federal hiring build - blocked, so I can show the current composition but cannot prove when it changed

The consumption-pricing shift ($250k three-month pilot / $500k initial production deployment / $0.55 per vCPU-hour) - real and it does depress near-term ACV, but it has been discussed on calls for years and was written up on 2026-08-31, so it is in the wire

Short interest at ~32.4% of float as of 2026-08-03 and a put/call OI ratio of 0.05 - genuinely extreme, but it is on every terminal and the OI leg is already inside my sealed baseline, so it is not a finding
baseline_tension: My net cuts only slightly against nothing: the negative leg agrees with the +19 vol-point skew, the 7.7% five-day run-up and six negative prints out of eight, which is precisely why I refuse to size it large - the one thing I found that genuinely disagrees with the priced downside bid, the funded defense/intelligence rebuild, is an option on tonight's narrative rather than a number, and against a 12.7% implied move on a bar cut to $50-54M from $70.3M with 32% of float short, the honest read is that the price already holds most of this.
